notes: Portable Bluetooth speaker, serial numbers starting GG per the service manual cover. Units changed in October 2019 to a Qualcomm Bluetooth module and a different battery part; the bulletin says the old and new modules are compatible but need the matching battery.

gaps: Battery capacity conflict: the spec page (which also gives 27 Wh) and JBL's product page say 7500 mAh, while the spare parts list (p.20) prints 7800 mAh for both battery parts. 7500 mAh is recorded; Wh is not put in w.
Battery part numbers EBA00037 (CSR units) and PAS01767001 (QCC units) are on p.20 and p.22 but are not in a comp, because the battery comp cites the spec page.
The parts list quantity column cannot be matched to rows (56 rows, one quantity of 2 not tied to a part), so no quantity is recorded for the speaker, microphone or LED board.
The spec page's 30 W RMS rated power is for the whole product, so no w is set on the speaker.

Page 13 is a schematic that could not be rendered here (ManualsLib refused a direct download with HTTP 403); the amplifier and DAC labels were read from the page text, where U300 and U301 are followed by the pin names of a 28-pin PCM512x and a 32-pin TPA3128D2.
The Bluetooth modules have no chip number in the manual, only the names 'JX BT Module' (CSR) and 'Sunitec BT Module' (Qualcomm QCC).
The 5 V / 2.3 A is the condition quoted for the 4-hour charge time, not a rating of the charging port, so no v or a is set. The DAC is filed under ic_audio as the closest part type.
Not claimed: charger IC, magnets, main board and key board chips.
method: Service manual for the JBL CHARGE 4 on ManualsLib (cover: harman/kardon, Inc., Ver. 2.1 Nov. 2019, 25 pages): p.2 specifications, p.13 circuit labels, p.20 spare parts list, p.22 service bulletin JBL2019-011.
JBL product page for the Charge 4 (kh.jbl.com): 7500 mAh battery, 30 W output power, 4 h charging time; second source for the battery capacity.
TI TPA3128D2 (SLOS941C) and PCM5121 (SLAS763C) datasheets opened and name the chips.
ManualsLib pages were read as text through the fetch tool; direct downloads got HTTP 403 and were not retried.

comps.spec: Lithium-ion polymer battery, 27 Wh, equivalent to 3.6 V, 7500 mAh (spec page; JBL's product page also gives 7500 mAh)
Dual passive radiators (spec page features list)
TPA3128D2 class-D amplifier IC, schematic reference U301
PCM5121 audio DAC IC, schematic reference U300 (filed under ic_audio as the closest part type)
Bluetooth module: CSR ('JX BT Module') in earlier units, Qualcomm QCC ('Sunitec BT Module') after the change in service bulletin JBL2019-011 (Oct. 2019)
Microphone, JBL part EMC00047, listed as MIC D4*1.5 L110mm
LED board, JBL part CCA00364011 (non-Japan) or PAS01770001 (Japan)
USB charging: the spec page gives a 4-hour charge time at 5 V / 2.3 A and a USB output for charging other devices of 5 V / 2 A maximum; a Type C USB cable is in the box
